title: Transport
levelNote: Six tiers in one file. A car and a bus are pictures a four year old already knows, and the same two nouns carry all the way up to the economics of a road jammed with them.
goal: Name types of transport and the people who drive them, buy a ticket, and talk about a journey.
goal_pt: Nomear meios de transporte e as pessoas que os conduzem, comprar uma passagem, e falar sobre uma viagem.

lines.text: Good morning! Is this the bus stop?
Yes, it is. The bus is red.
I like the bus. Is it fast?
Yes, very fast. Here it comes now!
Thank you! Goodbye!
Goodbye! Have a good trip!
Hello. One ticket to the city, please.
That's five pounds. Are you a passenger on the ten o'clock train?
Yes, that's right. Is it busy today?
A little. Do you have much luggage?
Just one bag, thank you.
Perfect. The train leaves from the station in ten minutes.
Thank you very much!

dialogue.title: A delayed flight at the airport

lines.text: Excuse me, is this flight delayed?
Yes, I'm afraid so. There is a delay of one hour.
Oh no. Have you checked the new time on the timetable?
I have. It now leaves at three o'clock, from terminal two.
Terminal two? I thought we were at terminal one.
They changed it this morning. Have you ever missed a flight before?
Once, a few years ago. I won't be late again.
Don't worry, we have plenty of time now.

questions.q: Which terminal does the flight leave from now?

reading.title: A trip to the airport
reading.text:
On Sunday my father takes me to the airport. We go by car. My father drives, and I look out of the window.

At the airport we see many planes. Some are big and some are small. I want to see a red plane, and we find one!

We do not fly today. We just watch the planes. Then we go home for lunch, happy and hungry.

reading.title: The morning train
reading.text:
Every weekday, Maria walks to the station near her house. The platform is often busy, and she has learned to stand near the middle, where the doors always open.

The journey into the city takes forty minutes, longer if there is trouble on the line. Maria uses the time to read or to look out at the towns going past. She has taken the same train for two years now, and she knows most of the other regular passengers by sight, even if she has never spoken to them.

Today the train is five minutes late, which barely counts as a delay. Maria checks the timetable on her phone, sees nothing to worry about, and goes back to her book.

reading.title: Why the road feels free and the train feels shared
reading.text:
A car gives the illusion of a journey nobody else controls: you choose the hour, the route, and the stops, and the only cost of a mistake is a wrong turn. A train offers something almost the opposite. The timetable, the platform, and the price are fixed by other people long before you arrive, and your only real decision is whether to be there on time.

It is tempting to call the car the free choice and the train the constrained one, but that gets the economics backwards. A road that feels free to one driver is only free because thousands of other drivers are not on it at that moment; add enough cars and the same road becomes the most rigid infrastructure imaginable, measured in minutes lost to congestion rather than freedom gained. A train, by contrast, gets more efficient as more people use it, up to a point, because the cost of running it barely changes whether it carries ten passengers or four hundred.

None of this means one is better than the other for every journey. It means that comfort with a form of transport, once you look closely, often has less to do with independence than with who else happens to be sharing the infrastructure that day, and how honest you are willing to be about that.

Bus is short and sharp. Don't add an extra sound at the end.

speaking.text: Have you ever flown on a plane?

speaking.text: The train was delayed by an hour.

speaking.text: Although it was delayed, we arrived on time.
speaking.tip: Pause after delayed, not after although.
